factors.name: Connectivity and branching
factors.summary: Measures of arcs per node and per connector load very highly here (Average connector degree 0.98, Token split 0.96, Coefficient of network connectivity 0.95, Control flow complexity 0.91, Maximum connector degree 0.88), so the factor captures how many arcs and splits a net has relative to its nodes. Number of empty sequence flows (0.74) and Connector Mismatch (0.59) also belong here but load more moderately, and both carry notable secondary loadings on Factor 2 (0.52 and 0.36).

factors.name: Size with sequential/separable structure
factors.summary: Separability (0.83) and Sequentiality (0.82) carry the factor, joined by Size (0.66) and weakly by Connector Heterogeneity (0.41, communality only 0.20). Larger nets with a higher share of plain arcs and of non-articulation nodes score high, but by their definitions these two measures do not obviously express one notion, so the name describes their co-variation in this dataset rather than an established construct. Size also loads 0.47 on Factor 1.

interpretation.overall: The data are suitable for factor analysis (Bartlett p < 0.001, overall KMO 0.81), and the eigenvalues (7.40, 1.47, 0.96) support the two retained factors, which together explain 77% of the variance (51% and 26% after varimax rotation). Factor 1 is a strong connectivity/branching dimension with very high loadings of arc- and connector-based measures. Factor 2 is weaker and combines Separability, Sequentiality and Size. All loadings are positive and several measures (Size, Number of empty sequence flows, Connector Mismatch) load substantially on both factors, so the separation between the two dimensions is not clean.
caveats: Density was removed by the MSA filter (MSA 0.44) and Number of duplicate tasks was constant, so the factors say nothing about these measures.
Size (0.47/0.66), Number of empty sequence flows (0.74/0.52) and Connector Mismatch (0.59/0.36) load on both factors even though their gaps exceed the 0.15 cross-loading rule.
Connector Heterogeneity has a communality of only 0.20 and is poorly explained by the solution; it is also undefined for nets without connectors.
The third eigenvalue (0.96) is close to 1, so a three-factor solution might split Factor 2 differently.
Separability has an MSA of 0.61, only just above the 0.6 threshold.
Communalities near 1 and eigenvalues near 0 indicate that several Factor 1 measures are nearly redundant in these 288 nets.
The factors reflect shared variance in this particular set of discovered nets under varimax rotation, not causal or generally valid dimensions.
